note: Draft cast for Carthage's home politics, 410 to 380 BC, in data/people.json's shape. Not wired into the game. Card: docs/drafts/carthage-cast.md; history records cite docs/research/carthage-government.md. 'faction' is one of Carthage's blocs in data/carthage.json (elders, hundred, people, libyans) and is always a game proposal. 'wants' is one of Carthage's goals there (rebuild, tribute, war, peace, libya). 'opinion' is of the ruler of Syracuse. 'status' outside means alive, in Carthage or Libya. 'general' and 'method' are the two extra fields that data/carthage.json gives its people; the ids himilcon, magon, hanno and bomilcar are the same people as there. 'enters' is the first season someone can appear (format season-year). The fields named in 'invented' are game invention.

people.name: Hannibal son of Gisco
people.role: Carthage's foremost citizen and general of 410 to 406
people.rivalNote: Dead before a 405 start (plague before Acragas, 406). Kept for an earlier start and to explain the family. His motive is the one Diodorus gives: his family's disgrace at Himera.

facts.text: Carthage's foremost citizen in 410/409.
facts.quote: Hannibal, their foremost citizen

facts.text: Chosen general while lawfully holding sovereign power.
facts.quote: they selected as general Hannibal, who at the time lawfully exercised sovereign powers

facts.text: In the Greek: king, according to the laws, at the time.
facts.quote: κατὰ νόμους τότε βασιλεύοντα

facts.text: Grandson of the general who died at Himera; son of an exile.
facts.quote: He was the grandson of Hamilcar, who fought in the war against Gelon and died at Himera, and the son of Gescon, who had been exiled because of his father's defeat

facts.text: Hated the Greeks and meant to wipe out his family's disgrace.
facts.quote: by nature was a hater of the Greeks and at the same time desired to wipe out the disgraces which had befallen his ancestors

facts.text: Killed some three thousand captives where his grandfather fell, 409.
facts.quote: he led to the spot where once his grandfather Hamilcar had been slain by Gelon

facts.text: Welcomed home in triumph, 409.
facts.quote: the whole city came out to meet him, paying him homage and honour

facts.text: Asked to be excused for his age, 406.
facts.quote: When he begged to be excused because of his age

facts.text: Died of plague before Acragas, 406.
facts.quote: Among the dead was also Hannibal the general

invented: status at a 405 start is history; the rest of the list is invention

people.name: Himilcon
people.role: General of Carthage; king for the war of 396
people.rivalNote: Same man as the game's Himilcon in data/carthage.json (traits, general and method kept). His home side: king in 396, home in rags the same year, judged himself, no trial.

facts.text: Son of Hanno, of Hannibal's family; made co-general in 406.
facts.quote: another general, Himilcon, the son of Hanno and of the same family

facts.text: Given supreme command for the war of 396.
facts.quote: lawfully according Himilcon sovereign power

facts.text: In the Greek: made king according to the law.
facts.quote: Ἰμίλκωνα βασιλέα κατὰ νόμον καταστήσαντες

facts.text: Fled by night with the citizens and left the rest of his army.
facts.quote: manned forty triremes during the night with the citizens of Carthage and began his flight, abandoning all the rest of his army

facts.text: Came home in disgrace.
facts.quote: slipped away in disgrace to Carthage with a few survivors

facts.text: Starved himself to death.
facts.quote: In the end he passed sentence of death upon himself and starved himself to death

facts.text: Came off his ship dressed as a slave (late source).
facts.quote: with his belt removed, and in a mean dress like that of a slave

facts.text: Shut his door, even on his sons, and ended his life (late source).
facts.quote: admitting no one, not even his sons, to his presence, he put an end to his life

people.name: Himilcon's son
people.role: A son of the disgraced general (no text names him)
grudges: his father's army died of plague before your walls and his father died of the shame, 396
people.rivalNote: Justin says only that Himilco had sons. Which son, his name, age and everything he does are invention. The grudge is invention built on history.

facts.text: Himilcon had sons (late source).
facts.quote: not even his sons

people.name: Magon
people.role: Admiral of Carthage in 396; general in 392; king in 383
people.entersNote: first named as Himilcon's admiral, about 396 (range 397 to 395)
people.rivalNote: Same man as the game's Magon in data/carthage.json (traits, general and method kept). The only man of these years who rises from admiral under a disgraced king to king.

facts.text: Himilcon's admiral, about 396.
facts.quote: he dispatched Magon his admiral with his naval armament

facts.text: Won the subject towns by kindness, about 393.
facts.quote: showed kindness to the subject cities and received the victims of Dionysius' wars

facts.text: Led a great army in 392.
facts.quote: no less than eighty thousand in number and under the command of Magon

facts.text: Sailed home after the peace of 392.
facts.quote: After the conclusion of the treaty Magon sailed off

facts.text: Chosen general as king for the war of 383/382.
facts.quote: As general they chose their king Magon

facts.text: Killed at Cabala.
facts.quote: There fell also Magon their king after a splendid combat

facts.text: Given a great funeral.
facts.quote: gave their king Magon a magnificent funeral

people.name: Magon's son
people.role: General after his father fell; victor at Cronium (no text names him)
people.entersNote: made general in the war Diodorus files under 383/382 (many modern accounts put it later, to about 375)
grudges: his father Magon was killed fighting your army at Cabala
people.rivalNote: Two traits follow Diodorus' words (ambition, courage); the rest is invention. The grudge is invention built on history.

facts.text: Made general when his father fell.
facts.quote: replaced him as general with his son, who, though he was young indeed, was full of ambition and distinguished for his courage

facts.text: Drilled the army through a truce.
facts.quote: He spent the entire period of the truce drilling and exercising his troops

facts.text: The truce was asked so the men in the field could consult the government at home.
facts.quote: in order that they might discuss the question with their government

facts.text: His peace made Dionysius pay.
facts.quote: Dionysius paid the Carthaginians one thousand talents

people.name: Suniatus
people.role: The most powerful man in Carthage, who wrote to Syracuse in Greek (one late source)
people.entersNote: Justin's order puts him about 387 to 383; Wikipedia dates the ban on Greek to 368, after these years
people.rivalNote: Known only from Justin, centuries later. He hated Hanno the general and betrayed his army's approach to Dionysius. In the game his letter could reach you as news, and be caught.

facts.text: The most powerful Carthaginian of his day, Hanno's enemy (late source).
facts.quote: whose enemy Suniatus, the most powerful of the Carthaginians at that time

facts.text: Wrote to Dionysius in Greek about the army and its slow general.
facts.quote: in a letter written in Greek, of the approach of the army and the inactivity of its leader

facts.text: The letter was caught; found guilty of treason.
facts.quote: was found, through the letter being intercepted, guilty of treason

facts.text: Then the senate banned the study of Greek.
facts.quote: that no Carthaginian should thenceforward study the Greek literature or language

people.name: Hanno the general
people.role: Leader of a Carthaginian expedition to Sicily (one late source; not Hanno the elder)
people.entersNote: as for Suniatus: Justin's order about 387 to 383, possibly the 360s
people.rivalNote: One sentence in Justin. Diodorus names Magon as general of the war of 383/382, so this may be another war or Justin's error. Not the invented Hanno the elder.

facts.text: Led the expedition (late source).
facts.quote: The leader in the expedition was Hanno the Carthaginian

facts.text: His enemy called him slow.
facts.quote: the inactivity of its leader

people.name: the leader of the Libyan rising
people.role: A leader of the Libyan rising of 396 (no text names one)
people.entersNote: the rising followed the disaster at Syracuse, 396 (range 397 to 395)
people.rivalNote: The rising is history; the man is unnamed, and Diodorus says the rebels had no capable commanders and quarrelled over the command. 'wants' here is the goal his rising forces on Carthage (Quiet Libya).

facts.text: The Libyans hated Carthage's rule, and more so after Syracuse.
facts.quote: who had long hated the oppressive rule of the Carthaginians and even more at this time because of the betrayal of the soldiers at Syracuse

facts.text: A very large rising (Diodorus' number).
facts.quote: a body of two hundred thousand men

facts.text: No capable commanders.
facts.quote: possessed no capable commanders

facts.text: Quarrels over the command; some leaders bought off.
facts.quote: they quarrelled among themselves over the supreme command and some of them were bought off with Carthaginian money

facts.text: The rising broke up.
facts.quote: broke up and scattered to their native lands

people.name: Hanno the elder
people.role: Head of a great merchant house, for the Elders
people.rivalNote: Already in the game (data/carthage.json), portrait in PR 95. No text names an Elder of these years other than the generals. Leans on Diodorus 14.47.2 (the council hears first) and Aristotle, Politics 2.11, 1273a (later: wealth chooses rulers).

people.name: Carthalo son of Hamilcar
people.role: An elder with ships in the western trade
grudges: the Syracusans plundered his ships in their harbour with your permission, 398/397
people.rivalNote: Invented. Leans on Diodorus 14.46.1: Carthaginians lived at Syracuse and their merchants' ships were plundered with Dionysius' leave. The grudge is invention built on that.

people.name: Sibbolet daughter of Hamilcar
people.role: Runs her brother Carthalo's warehouse; trades with Greeks
people.rivalNote: Invented. Her name is a businesswoman's on an undated gravestone at Carthage (docs/research/punic-womens-names.md). Leans on Diodorus 14.77.5 (Greeks living at Carthage). A ban on Greek (Justin 20.5.13, late) would cut her trade.

people.name: Maharbal son of Carthalo
people.role: An elder sent abroad with silver to hire armies; lends to the state
people.rivalNote: Invented. Leans on Diodorus 13.80.2 and 14.47.3 (esteemed citizens and senators sent abroad with silver to hire men) and 13.62.5 (the Campanians' complaint about their reward).

people.name: Adherbal son of Sapho
people.role: An elder who owns estates in Libya
people.rivalNote: Invented. Leans on Diodorus 13.114.2 (plague in Libya, 405) and 14.77.1 to 14.77.6 (the rising of 396, slaves among the rebels, leaders bought off).

people.name: Bostar son of Malchus
people.role: A suffete of the year
people.rivalNote: Invented. No suffete of these years is named, and yearly suffetes in 405 are disputed (docs/research/carthage-government.md, section 1). Leans on Aristotle, Politics 2.11, 1273a (later): the kings and Elders decide what goes to the people.

people.name: Hasdrubal son of Bostar
people.role: A priest of Demeter and Kore, the new goddesses of 396
people.entersNote: the priesthood was founded after the disaster of 396
people.rivalNote: Invented. Leans on Diodorus 14.77.4 to 14.77.5: Carthage made its most renowned citizens priests of the two goddesses and gave Greeks living there a part in the rites.

people.name: Bomilcar
people.role: A man of the Hundred who wants a command
people.rivalNote: Already in the game (data/carthage.json), portrait in PR 95. Not the Bomilcar of 308, who is later. Leans on Aristotle, Politics 2.11, 1273a (later): the generalship could be bought.

people.name: Synalus son of Adherbal
people.role: A judge of the Hundred who audits the generals
people.rivalNote: Invented. No court sits in any text of 410 to 380. Leans on Justin 19.2.5 to 19.2.6 (late: a hundred judges to demand an account from returning generals) and Aristotle, Politics 2.11, 1272b (later: the Hundred and Four, elected by merit).

people.name: Annobal son of Malchus
people.role: A speaker of the craftsmen in the people's assembly
people.rivalNote: Invented. No speaker of the people is named in these years. Leans on Diodorus 14.47.2 (the letter read to the people) and 14.77.4 (the city in terror), and Aristotle, Politics 2.11, 1273a (later: anyone may speak against a proposal). His name is from an inscription of AD 1 to 2.

people.name: Bodostor son of Bodashtart
people.role: A speaker of the dockyards in the people's assembly
people.rivalNote: Invented. Leans on Diodorus 14.54.5 (Ephorus' four hundred warships for 396) and 14.76.2 (the fleet burned before Syracuse).

people.name: Zarzas son of Muttines
people.role: First man of a Libyan town under Carthage
people.rivalNote: Invented. Leans on Diodorus 13.44.1 (Libyans in Carthage's armies) and 14.77.6 (rebel leaders bought off). Both names are of much later Libyans who served Carthage.
